concept: An execution plan shows how SQL Server chooses to access and combine data. Indexes can accelerate selective lookups but have storage and write costs.
example:
CREATE INDEX IX_Orders_CustomerID_OrderDate
ON dbo.Orders (CustomerID, OrderDate)
INCLUDE (Amount);

SELECT OrderDate, Amount
FROM dbo.Orders
WHERE CustomerID = 42
  AND OrderDate >= '2026-01-01';
breakdown: The composite key starts with CustomerID, matching an equality predicate.
OrderDate is next, supporting the range predicate within that customer.
INCLUDE (Amount) may cover the SELECT without an extra lookup.
Use the actual execution plan and logical reads to evaluate benefit; do not assume an index always wins.
practice: Explain why an index on (OrderDate, CustomerID) might be less useful for this particular predicate pattern. Name two measurements you would check.
takeaways: Compare plans and IO before and after changes; test on representative data.

A list of all future database transactions.
